## Ready-made automations

Three blueprints, imported with one click from the README and set up in the
Home Assistant UI without YAML:

- **Run a device on a plan** - heat pump, water heater or EV charger on while
  a plan or window is active, off when it ends, with a choice of what to do
  while no plan exists yet.
- **Start an appliance at the cheapest time before a deadline** - load the
  dishwasher, switch a "ready" helper on, and it starts in the cheapest stretch
  that is still finished by, say, 07:00. Unlike the cheapest window, which
  searches the whole forecast and can be days away, it stays inside your
  deadline.
- **Tell me what tomorrow costs** - once a day, tomorrow's average, cheapest
  and dearest time, and whether that is the published price or still the
  forecast; optionally only when tomorrow is expensive.

## Home batteries: EMHASS and Predbat

A new page shows how to feed both optimisers from this integration, so they
plan with the forecast beyond tomorrow's published prices - up to five days
with Private Pro. Predbat needs a small template sensor for that, which the
page gives in full.

## Forecast quarters follow the curve

Where the market trades in quarter hours, forecast hours used to arrive as
four identical quarter values. The API now draws them on a straight line
through the hourly forecast values, so a rising evening price is a ramp, not
a staircase. Measured over 30 autumn days, that lowered the error per quarter
hour in Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and West Denmark on 26 to 30 days out
of 30, and made the chosen four-hour window cheaper on average. It does not
add information about short spikes within an hour. Published prices and
hourly tariffs are unchanged. This happens on the server, so it applies with
any version.

## Smaller things

- The dashboard card's "Exchange price" tile now says that it is the price
  now and what fees and taxes make of it, instead of standing next to retail
  figures unexplained.
- On the day the clocks went back, the published forecast for Central Europe
  missed one of the two 02:00 hours (issue #6). That was fixed on the server
  on 28 and 29 October for all affected markets, with tests for both changes of time.

## What do you switch with it?

The integration is used quietly, which is fine, but it means we are guessing
which automations to build next. If you have a minute: what do you control
with it - heat pump, EV, battery, dishwasher, something else - and what would
you like it to decide for you? One line in
[Discussions](https://github.com/BackupBaTTerY/energypriceforecast-home-assistant/discussions/categories/general-feedback-and-experiences-with-the-integration)
helps a lot.
